# Acoustic references and design translation

The package contains no copied samples. Every WAV is rendered by the included
C89 synthesizer. Public recordings were used only as qualitative listening
references; research papers supplied the main acoustic model.

## Rocket priority

### NASA SP-8072: Acoustic Loads Generated by the Propulsion System

https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/19710023719/downloads/19710023719.pdf

NASA describes rocket acoustic loading as a broad-frequency field created by
exhaust mixing with the atmosphere. The principal source is fluctuating
turbulence distributed along the exhaust-mixing region; radiation is strongly
directional, and ordinary rocket noise is broadband rather than a single
discrete tone.

Translation into v1.2:

- the filtered plume-noise branch remains essential;
- the pure sine is reduced from sole carrier to one component of the sound;
- short unequal stereo air delays suggest an extended, directional source;
- the whistle layer is treated as game-readable trajectory information rather
  than a literal claim that real rocket exhaust is a musical oscillator.

## Pyrotechnic-whistle character

### Investigation on the acoustic properties of pyrotechnic whistles

https://www.jes.or.jp/mag/stem/Vol.80/documents/Vol.80%2CNo.4%2Cp.130-135.pdf

The measurements show a strong fundamental with higher harmonics. One measured
case identifies peaks near 4.834, 9.668 and 14.502 kHz. The paper also describes
a period of random gas-flow noise before a stable whistle forms, followed by a
frequency decrease as the effective resonating chimney changes.

Translation into v1.2:

- weak second and third harmonics;
- delayed filtered air rather than an immediate clean tone;
- bounded pitch and amplitude irregularity;
- a release whose frequency falls while the air tail remains audible.

### Effect of particle size of ingredients on acoustic behavior of a
pyrotechnic whistle

https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/stem/84/1/84_9/_pdf

The 2023 paper reports a harmonic series with frequency ratios 1, 2, 3 and so
on, and models the resonating gas column similarly to an organ pipe.

Translation into v1.2: harmonic phases are generated directly from the base
trajectory frequency, but at restrained levels in weapon presets. The separate
chifladora reference preset exaggerates this relationship for comparison.

## Public audio/video references

### Mexican chiflador compilation

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2OG5XKLDjyM

The public video was located as an informal reference for the airy, spatial and
slightly unstable quality associated with Mexican "chifladores". Naming and
construction vary locally, so the included preset is labeled as a reference,
not as a standardized product model.

### Whistling firework sound-effects compilation

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zxHSkdwfK_c

Used only as a secondary qualitative comparison for the ratio between narrow
whistle energy and diffuse high-frequency air. No audio is bundled or copied.

### DVIDS: SMAW and AT-4 live-fire exercise

https://www.dvidshub.net/video/416461/9th-esb-combat-engineers-launch-rockets-destroy-targets-with-smaw-4-weapon-systems

Official exercise footage was used qualitatively to keep weapon-oriented
presets grounded in launch impulse, short flight duration and outdoor decay.
The trajectory-whistle library does not replace the separate blast, backblast,
mechanical or impact layers in a complete weapon synth engine.

## Important limitations

The validation environment could inspect the papers and public media pages but
could not reliably download the reference media tracks for automated spectral
measurement. Therefore:

- no claim of sample-accurate matching is made;
- no reference recording is copied into the package;
- final tuning combines published acoustic behavior, qualitative media
  comparison and synthetic listening tests;
- the chifladora preset is intentionally more exaggerated than the six
  missile/rocket presets.
